clat_ug_omr.stage_name: CLAT Undergraduate (BA LLB / BBA LLB) Offline Written Examination

sections.name: English Language
sections.scope: Passages of around 450 words derived from contemporary and historically significant fiction and non-fiction writing. Focus on reading comprehension, central themes, inferences, word meanings, metaphors, and grammatical syntax.

sections.name: Current Affairs, including General Knowledge
sections.scope: Passages derived from news articles, journalistic sources, non-fiction writing covering contemporary events in India and the world, arts and culture, international affairs, historical events of ongoing significance, and public policy.

sections.name: Legal Reasoning
sections.scope: Passages relating to legal matters, public policy questions, moral philosophical inquiries. Evaluation of candidate's ability to identify legal principles from facts, apply legal rules to scenarios, and evaluate changes in application.

sections.name: Logical Reasoning
sections.scope: Short passages evaluating ability to recognize arguments, premises and conclusions, identify patterns of reasoning, assess strengths and weaknesses, draw inferences, and identify logical fallacies.

sections.name: Quantitative Techniques
sections.scope: Short sets of facts or propositions, textual representations of numerical information, followed by questions requiring derivation, manipulation, and application of mathematical operations (10th standard arithmetic, ratios, percentages, mensuration, data analysis).

subjects.name: English Language & Reading Comprehension (अंग्रेजी भाषा एवं बोध)
domains: Reading Comprehension: Identifying central idea, main theme, and supporting arguments in discursive and argumentative passages
Inference and Deduction: Drawing logical inferences and conclusions based on contextual clues
Vocabulary in Context: Contextual word meanings, archaic and specialized terminology, antonyms, synonyms
Idiomatic Expressions & Figurative Language: Metaphors, similes, irony, paradox, analogies in prose
Author's Tone and Perspective: Objective, analytical, critical, satirical, appreciative, polemical
Structural Analysis: Paragraph organization, transitions, sentence re-arrangements, cohesion
Grammar & Syntax Mastery: Subject-verb agreement, modifier placement, parallel structure, conditional clauses
Critical Reading: Distinguishing facts from opinions, identifying underlying assumptions in textual rhetoric

subjects.name: Current Affairs & General Knowledge (समसामयिक घटनाएं एवं सामान्य ज्ञान)
domains: National Current Events: Landmark judicial rulings, legislative enactments, policy reforms, constitutional amendments
International Affairs & Geopolitics: UN bodies, multilateral treaties, bilateral summits, global conflicts, diplomatic conventions
Economic Developments: Union Budget, monetary policy directives, global economic institutions (IMF, World Bank, WTO), inflation indicators
Science, Technology & Environment: Space missions, climate summits (COP declarations), AI policy frameworks, renewable energy transitions
Historical & Cultural Heritage: Indian freedom movement, constitutional history, cultural landmarks, archaeological discoveries
Awards, Honors & Sports: Nobel Prizes, Bharat Ratna, Gallantry awards, Olympic and international sports championships
Social Issues & Human Rights: Socio-economic indices, SDG rankings, human rights covenants, public health and education initiatives
Legal & Constitutional Current Affairs: Collegium decisions, Law Commission reports, landmark Supreme Court constitutional bench hearings

subjects.name: Legal Reasoning, Constitutional Law & Jurisprudence (विधिक अभिक्षमता, संवैधानिक विधि एवं विधिशास्त्र)
domains: Constitutional Law: Fundamental Rights (Articles 12-35), Directive Principles of State Policy, Basic Structure doctrine, Judicial review
Law of Torts: Negligence, Nuisance, Defamation, Trespass, Strict liability (Rylands v. Fletcher), Absolute liability (M.C. Mehta case)
Law of Contracts: Offer and Acceptance, Consideration, Capacity to contract, Free consent (Coercion, Undue influence, Fraud, Misrepresentation), Breach and Damages
Criminal Law & Penal Code: Mens Rea and Actus Reus, General Exceptions (Private defense, Insanity, Intoxication), Offences against body (Homicide, Murder) and property (Theft, Extortion)
Family Law & Personal Laws: Marriage, Divorce, Maintenance, Adoption, Succession across personal legal frameworks and Uniform Civil Code principles
Environmental Law: Precautionary principle, Polluter pays principle, Public trust doctrine, National Green Tribunal jurisdiction
Intellectual Property Rights: Copyrights, Patents, Trademarks, Geographical indications, Fair dealing provisions
Legal Maxims & Terminology: Volenti non fit injuria, Res ipsa loquitur, Nemo judex in causa sua, Audi alteram partem, Actus non facit reum nisi mens sit rea
Application of Legal Principles: Fact-principle-reasoning analysis, applying codified rules strictly without bringing external personal prejudices

subjects.name: Logical Reasoning, Critical Thinking & Quantitative Techniques (तार्किक क्षमता, गहन चिंतन एवं परिमाणात्मक तकनीकें)
domains: Critical Reasoning: Identifying arguments, identifying premises, unstated assumptions, and logical conclusions
Argument Evaluation: Strengthening and weakening arguments, identifying flaws in reasoning, parallel reasoning patterns
Deductive & Analytical Reasoning: Categorical propositions, syllogisms, conditional statements (Modus Ponens, Modus Tollens)
Logical Relations & Analogies: Cause and effect relationships, course of action, assertions and reasons
Data Interpretation: Reading and deriving insights from short caselets, numerical passages, tabular charts, bar graphs
Arithmetic Fundamentals: Ratios and Proportions, Percentages, Profit and Loss, Simple and Compound Interest, Averages
Time, Speed, Distance & Work: Rates of work, relative speed, travel time calculations applied in practical scenarios
Mensuration & Statistical Estimation: Basic geometric measurements, perimeter, area, volume, median, mean, statistical data evaluation
